references.text: Psalm 23 describes the Lord as a shepherd who leads his people to safe pastures ("green pastures") and protects them, which is the direct image Jesus uses when he promises that those who enter through him will find "pasture" (νομὴν).

Ezekiel 34 contains a prophecy in which God himself promises to become the shepherd of shepherds, lead his people out and in, and let them find pasture—a direct parallel to Jesus' self-understanding as the door that grants access to salvation and pasture.

In the same book (John), Jesus declares that he is the way, the truth, and the life, and that no one comes to the Father except through him, which is a theological elaboration of the claim that he is the door to salvation.

The context in John 10:1–2 describes anyone who does not enter through the door but climbs over as a thief, while whoever enters through the door is the shepherd, establishing the door as the only valid point of entry.
